questions.question: A promise is…
options: A receipt for a value that might not be ready
A callback registry that runs inside the caller
Only the return type of fetch
questions.explanation: then registers work for when it settles. Already settled promises still run then later.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: A promise is a receipt representing a value that may not be available yet.

questions.question: Order of: log("sync"); Promise.resolve().then(() => log("promise")); setTimeout(() => log("timeout"), 0);
questions.explanation: The current stack finishes, then promise reactions, then timers.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Promises always resolve or reject as a new event.

questions.question: then on a promise returns…
options: A new promise for the callback result
questions.explanation: That is how a chain waits on a promise returned from a callback.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: A useful thing about the then method is that it itself returns another promise.

questions.question: If a then callback throws, the promise returned by then…
questions.explanation: A throw in a reaction is a rejection of the next promise.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: rejection when they throw an exception, and the outcome of the promise when they return a promise.

questions.question: Calling an async function…
options: Runs it to the end on this stack before you continue
Throws synchronously if the function throws
questions.explanation: return 1 fulfills that promise. throw rejects it. The caller must await or then.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: When such a function or method is called, it returns a promise.

questions.question: await inside an async function…
options: Blocks every other script on the page until it finishes
Pauses that function and lets other turns run
Converts a rejection into a return value of null
questions.explanation: await on a plain value wraps it. await on a rejection throws into the async function, which rejects its promise unless you catch.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: An async function is marked by the word async before the function keyword.

questions.question: try { setTimeout(() => { throw new Error("Woosh"); }, 20); } catch (e) {} …
questions.explanation: The book: the catch will not run. The callback starts on an empty stack.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke

questions.question: A while loop that burns 50ms after scheduling a 20ms timeout…
options: Lets the timeout run at 20ms, in parallel
Delays the timeout until the loop finishes
questions.explanation: One turn at a time. The loop is the turn. The timer waits.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt:
while (Date.now() < start + 50) {}
 console.log("Wasted time until", Date.now() - start);

questions.question: Promise.all of three request promises…
options: Fulfills with the first result only
Fulfills with an array of results in input order
Runs the requests one at a time
questions.explanation: One rejection rejects the combined promise. The others are not cancelled.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Promise has a static method all that can be used to convert an array of promises into a single promise that resolves to an array of results.

questions.question: Promise.all([]) …
questions.explanation: There is no input that can reject.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Promise has a static method all that can be used to convert an array of promises into a single promise that resolves to an array of results.

questions.question: await inside a for loop versus Promise.all(items.map(...))
options: They start the work the same way
The loop waits for each step; map plus all can overlap
The loop is a syntax error
questions.explanation: Use the loop when the next call needs the previous result. Use all when the calls are independent.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Promise has a static method all that can be used to convert an array of promises into a single promise that resolves to an array of results.

questions.question: How do you catch a rejection from await read(path)?
options: try/catch around the call that created the promise, after you have already left the function
try/catch around the await, inside the async function
questions.explanation: await turns rejection into a throw in that function.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke

questions.question: read(path).then(handler) with no catch, when read rejects…
options: Becomes a normal return of undefined
Is an unhandled rejection unless something later catches that chain
questions.explanation: Attach catch, or await it inside try.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke

questions.question: Promise.resolve(1).then(() => 2) fulfills with…
questions.explanation: The callback return becomes the next result. The original value is the callback argument, which this arrow ignores.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: A useful thing about the then method is that it itself returns another promise.

questions.question: An async function that returns Promise.resolve(5) causes the caller's await to see…
questions.explanation: await and then flatten a returned promise one level.
